docRequirement: skills.md:124 — "Skills also load from nested `.claude/skills/` directories below your working directory. When Claude reads or edits a file in a subdirectory, skills from that subdirectory's `.claude/skills/` become available." :154 restates the timing: those skills "aren't loaded at startup. They load the first time Claude reads or edits a file inside that subdirectory, and stay available for the rest of the session" — and until then they "don't appear in autocomplete and can't be invoked by name". On a name clash with a root skill, :126 "both stay available"; :128 "The nested one appears under a directory-qualified name, `apps/web:deploy`"; :132 "Typing `/deploy` runs the project-root skill. Type the qualified name `/apps/web:deploy` to run the nested variant explicitly." Three bound behaviours: a descendant scan triggered by a file touch, a `<dir>:<name>` qualified name, and retention of BOTH variants (the unqualified name staying with the root one).
current: Skill discovery is eager and ancestor-only. `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` walks `ancestorsUpTo(workingDirectory, context.projectRoot)` and reads `<dir>/.agents/skills` at each level (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:1063-1066); `ancestorsUpTo` moves strictly upward via `dirname` (native-sources.ts:730-742). The Nessy-native tier reads `<workingDirectory>/.nessy-agent/skills` at the cwd only (native-sources.ts:1013-1016; `NESSY_AGENT_PROJECT_DIR = '.nessy-agent'`, packages/shared/src/projects/nessy-agent-layout.ts:12). `skillRecords` lists one directory's immediate children and is non-recursive (native-sources.ts:266-310, `readdirSync` at :276 with no `recursive` option). Those five `skillRecords(` call sites (native-sources.ts:903, :904, :949, :1016, :1065) are the complete set and none takes a descendant directory. `PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR = '.agents/skills'` (packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:37) — `.claude/skills` is never read as a skill source at all (`grep -ran` over packages/ and apps/ hits only comments in packages/shared/src/config/bundled-skills-settings.ts:12,22, packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:660 and packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/capabilities.ts:191,522, plus an unrelated SDK error string at packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:2272). A lazy, file-touch-triggered delivery channel DOES exist and is deliberately scoped to instruction files: `BaseAgent.getPathScopedRulePreToolUseContext` composes `cache.pathScopedRules + cache.pathGatedSkills + nestedInstructionProbe()` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:1152-1187), the probe matches `**/*` under the cwd (base-agent.ts:1206-1219), and the activation runs `discoverNestedInstructionFiles` (base-agent.ts:1230-1278), whose loop iterates `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES` only (native-sources.ts:845). Nothing in it looks for a skills directory. `pathGatedSkills` on that same list are skills ALREADY in the inventory whose `paths:` frontmatter gates model invocation (base-agent.ts:1062-1070, :2145-2151) — not discovery. No directory-qualified skill name exists anywhere: the model-facing reference is `skill.selectedAsUnqualifiedAlias ? skill.logicalName : skill.key` (packages/shared/src/agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:121-123), i.e. the bare slug or the raw internal key `skill::project::<workspaceId>::<projectKey>::d1::deploy` built by `qualifiedKey` (native-sources.ts:250-264); `resolveSkillReferences` accepts exactly that key, a bare alias only when it contains no `:`, or `<workspaceId>:<alias>` (base-agent.ts:2124-2136), so the literal form `apps/web:deploy` resolves to nothing. On a name clash the resolver does keep every duplicate and picks one unqualified-alias winner by scope specificity then tier (`applyCollisionPolicy`, packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:2011-2063), but the user-facing `/` menu then drops the loser outright: `selectSkillSlashCommands` skips any skill whose `logicalName` is already taken and emits no qualified entry (packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:436-456, the `taken.has(skill.logicalName)` guard at :444).
divergence: The descendant half of discovery is entirely absent — this is a missing scan plus a missing trigger, not a wrong key name. Three deltas: (1) no code path ever reads a skills directory BELOW the working directory, so `apps/web/.agents/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` is never inventoried when the session starts at the repo root; (2) no first-touch lazy skill load — the one lazy channel that exists (`nestedInstructionProbe` -> `discoverNestedInstructionFiles`) is hard-wired to `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES` and has no skill branch; (3) no directory-qualified name — the collision loser is addressable only by its internal capability key in the model listing and is not addressable at all from the `/` menu, where the doc requires `apps/web:deploy` / `/apps/web:deploy`. The adjacent mechanism the fork does have, `paths:` frontmatter on a root skill (native-sources.ts:301 -> base-agent.ts:1062 -> :2148), expresses "this root skill applies while working under apps/web" but not "apps/web owns its own skill directory", and it cannot be authored by the package that owns the subtree.

change.what: Add `discoverNestedSkillRoots(triggerFilePath, workingDirectory, options)` modelled line-for-line on `discoverNestedInstructionFiles:818-856` — same `isBelow:859` containment walk, same outermost-first reversal — returning, for each directory strictly between the trigger file and the cwd, the existing `<dir>/.agents/skills` and `<dir>/.nessy-agent/skills` paths. Bound it with a `MAX_NESTED_SKILL_ROOTS` constant declared beside `MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILES:764` (8 is the precedent). Extend the `NativeSourcesEnv` seam at :57-66 with `nestedSkillRoots?: readonly string[]` and, inside the trusted-project branch (:1012-1066), emit each supplied root through the EXISTING `skillRecords(root, projectScope, `nested:${relative(workingDirectory, dir)}`, projectRealRoot)` — the `projectRealRoot` containment argument is mandatory so a symlinked nested dir cannot escape the project. Set a new `skillDirectoryQualifier` field on those records to the cwd-relative directory (`apps/web`). Do not touch `ancestorsUpTo:730`; the upward walk stays as-is.
Add optional `skillDirectoryQualifier?: string`, carrying the working-directory-relative directory that owns a nested skill. Optional so every existing record and fixture stays valid.
Add `directoryQualifier?: string` to the handle and copy `s.skillDirectoryQualifier` through in the `case 'skill'` push, alongside the existing `skillPaths` spread at :195.

A record carrying `skillDirectoryQualifier` must never win the unqualified alias — skills.md:132 pins `/deploy` to the project-root skill. Add a rank term below `scopeSpecificity` that sorts qualified (nested) skills last for alias selection only; retention is already correct (every duplicate is kept, :2044-2053). Also propagate the qualifier onto `ResolvedCapability` (the summary built at :1646 / :1931) so views.ts can read it.

Two edits. (a) Discovery trigger: reuse the SAME `**/*` probe rather than adding a second — in the `onActivated` branch at :1174, alongside `activateNestedInstructionFiles`, call a new `activateNestedSkillRoots(generation, activation.triggerFilePath)` that runs `discoverNestedSkillRoots` and accumulates roots into a SESSION-lifetime set (the existing `nestedInstructionActivations` tracker is generation-scoped and reset at :1235, but skills.md:154 says nested skills "stay available for the rest of the session"), then requests a capability invalidation so the next snapshot includes them. Keep the `projectTrustState !== 'trusted'` guard at :1209 — nested skills are repository-owned content. (b) Invocation: `resolveSkillReferences` must accept `<qualifier>:<logicalName>`; today the guard at :2133 (`!reference.includes(':')`) rejects any reference containing a colon that is not an exact key or a `<workspaceId>:` prefix, so `apps/web:deploy` resolves to `missing`.

Return `${skill.directoryQualifier}:${skill.logicalName}` when the handle carries a qualifier, instead of falling through to the raw capability key. NOTE the constraint the comment at :424-427 and #862 record: the listing rides the STABLE context part inside Pi's cached system prefix, so a nested skill appearing mid-session re-stamps that prefix once per newly-touched subtree. Decide explicitly between accepting that one-off re-stamp and delivering the nested entry on the pending user-tail queue the way `activateNestedInstructionFiles` does at base-agent.ts:1261.

Replace the silent drop at :444 for a qualified skill: when `taken.has(skill.logicalName)` and the skill has a `directoryQualifier`, emit `name`/`label` as `<qualifier>:<name>` / `/<qualifier>:<name>` and `body` = `skillSlashCommandBody(reference)` with the same qualified reference, so skills.md:132's `/apps/web:deploy` works. `skillSlashCommandId:285` should key off the qualified name too, or two nested variants of one slug collide on id. `boundedIdentity` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:80-85) already admits `/` and `:` in a persisted invocation `name`, so no snapshot-validation change is needed.

Thread the session's accumulated nested skill roots into `deps.nativeSourcesEnv` at :641 so the per-turn rebuild keeps them. The safe-mode short-circuit at :630 must still win — a nested root is repository content and must not be read in safe mode.

Hold the activated nested-skill-root set on `ManagedSession` (the agent-side runtime is cleared after every turn at :5900) and pass it into the inputs builder on each `createCapabilityTurn:5881`. Clear it when the session's working directory changes.

Mirror `packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/nested-instruction-discovery.test.ts` (26-157): a root skill plus `apps/web/.agents/skills/deploy` — absent before any touch, present after a touch under `apps/web`, unqualified `/deploy` still resolving to the root variant, `apps/web:deploy` resolving to the nested one, a trigger outside the cwd returning nothing (that file's :122 case), and the `MAX_NESTED_SKILL_ROOTS` bound.

blastRadius: Discovery: `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` (native-sources.ts:880) has exactly one production caller, `buildCapabilityResolutionInputsV2` (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:634-643), which runs on EVERY capability turn through `SessionManager.withCapabilityRuntime` (SessionManager.ts:5871-5911) — so any per-touch growth of the scan set is paid per turn and must be bounded and memoized. Naming: `skillListingReference` (prompt-builder.ts:121) feeds the STABLE context part folded into Pi's cached system prefix — a changing listing re-stamps it and invalidates downstream history (#862, recorded in the comment at prompt-builder.ts:388-392 and :424-427); this is the sharpest risk in the change. Invocation: `resolveSkillReferences` (base-agent.ts:2115) is shared by the user path (`extractSkillInvocations:2279`) and the model path (`extractModelSkillInvocations`), so a reference-form change affects both at once. Persistence boundary — YES, it crosses one: a materialized invocation is frozen into a `SkillInvocationRecord` carrying `key` and `name` (runtime-skill-content.ts:882-889) and re-validated on restore by `validateSkillInvocationSnapshot` (:278-297), whose identity check compares `key`/`sourceDigest`/`generation`. New nested records get NEW keys (the `nested:<rel>` discriminator in `qualifiedKey`, native-sources.ts:250), so old snapshots stay valid — but changing the discriminator of an ALREADY-shipped record would break restore, so the ancestor discriminators `d${depth}` and `na` must not be touched. Wire boundary: skill-derived slash commands cross RPC to the composer via `listCustomSlashCommandSummaries` (SessionManager.ts:16016-16048) and `CustomSlashCommand`; a name containing `/` and `:` reaches the renderer's command matcher. Collision policy (`applyCollisionPolicy`, resolver.ts:2011) is shared by every non-MCP capability kind — a rank term added there must be gated on `kind === 'skill'` or it silently reorders agents, commands and output styles. Also read the same handle: `packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts` (materialization, `paths` gate), `packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:299-322` (the Sources/Skills UI rows), and the tests at `packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/runtime-skill-content.test.ts` and `packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-context.test.ts`, which build `RuntimeSkillHandle` literals.
userImpact: Concrete and reachable today. In a monorepo session opened at the repo root, a skill that a package owns — `apps/web/.agents/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` or `apps/web/.nessy-agent/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` — never becomes available, no matter how many files under `apps/web` the agent reads or edits. It is absent from the `<available_skills>` block the model sees (prompt-builder.ts:403), absent from the `/` command menu (SessionManager.ts:16038), and typing `/deploy` or `[skill:deploy]` resolves to nothing or to the root variant. The user's only options are to reopen the session with its working directory inside `apps/web`, or to move the skill to the project root and gate it with `paths:`. Second, smaller surface, present even without nested support: when two skills DO share a slug across the ancestor layers, the losing one is dropped from the `/` menu entirely (custom-commands.ts:444) rather than offered under a qualified name — the user sees one `/deploy` and has no way to reach the other except by typing the internal capability key `[skill:skill::project::<workspaceId>::<projectKey>::d1::deploy]`, which is neither documented nor shown anywhere in the UI.
